# Sunflower Oil

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the sunflower Oil came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-sunflower-oil" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-sunflower-oil-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of sunflower oil, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach sunflower Oil

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach sunflower Oil comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Sunflower Oil, oil from unrefined had Cu higher at 79.5 µg/kg, against 3.23 µg/kg for refined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="what-conclusions-require-finished-product-measurements-or-a-separate-exposure-assessment"></a>

No source in the library converted sunflower Oil concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

Every source record that names sunflower Oil was decided on its content: 14 occurrence extracted, 14 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

## Sunflower Oil FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-sunflower-oil" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-sunflower-oil" data-question="How do heavy metals get into sunflower Oil?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into sunflower Oil?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, sunflower Oil from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than sunflower Oil from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Sunflower Oil, oil from unrefined had lead higher at 16.2 µg/kg, against 0.675 µg/kg for refined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-sunflower-oil-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-sunflower-oil-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in sunflower Oil is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in sunflower Oil is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 4 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Assessment of metal levels in foodstuffs from the Region of Valencia (Spain)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 654-670</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Marín et al. 2018 reported inorganic arsenic at 2.8 µg/kg (mean) in sunflower Oil, oil from Vegetable oils group, Region of Valencia TDS 2010-2011.<sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D,
